utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, could you please bring in the accused? (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can everyone hear me? First of all, I would like to greet the interpreters. I hope everybody is ready, and we are now going to continue with the cross-examination, as soon as Brigadier Zeko will come and join us. Yes, Ivica Zeko. Let me just seize this occasion, after this witness, our colleague, Olivier Fourmy, has informed me of a number of points, and I would like to know how far we have gone with our schedule from now to the end of the year. I think that we can have a small Status Conference on this matter before the next witness comes in, an informal Status Conference, either just before the next witness comes in, and Mr. Olivier Fourmy will be with us. Is the witness ready? (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you hear me, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You may be seated. If you have rested, we can proceed now. Thank you. Mr. Harmon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good morning, Brigadier Zeko.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, did the HVO in Central Bosnia mount offensive operations against the Serbs in 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did they mount offence operations against the Serbs in 1993 in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They had frontlines with the Serbs, yes, but they did not undertake any offensive actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, before the HVO mounted offensive operations against the Serbs in 1992, did your intelligence operation provide intelligence information to Colonel Blaskic before each of those offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Those operations were mostly holding those current frontlines, but there were not any major operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The type of intelligence operation that you furnished to Colonel Blaskic before the operations against the Serb positions, can you tell us what kind of information that included?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Well, those were the status and the deployment of the enemy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you say "the status and deployment," you mean where the enemy was located, in which positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What else do you mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Where they were and how the units were deployed along those lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, did Colonel Blaskic routinely request that kind of information from you before he mounted an operation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Just one correction, please. You were mentioning Colonel Blaskic, whether he asked that from me. I was the deputy head of the staff for intelligence. I would always report to my superior, and then he would have his duties towards the head of the operational centre of Central Bosnia. So I carried out my duties, regardless of the fact whether any operations were to be mounted or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who is the head of your intelligence section? You said you were the deputy. Who was the head of it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The head of the intelligence department in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia was I, but in the staff, the head of the staff of the headquarters to which I belong was Franjo Nakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, my question to you, Brigadier, was did Colonel Blaskic routinely request intelligence information from you before he mounted an operation?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I don't recall whether I had any tasks like that, any requests of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me turn your attention to the visual aids and this very impressive visual production that you have testified about. Did you prepare these aids yourself?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. I prepared everything on the maps and on paper, and I gave it to the Defence team.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On what did you rely to prepare these various visual aids?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I relied on my notes, the notes that I made during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you rely on any other documents, besides the notes that you made during the war?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mostly the notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What else did you rely on, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said mostly on the notes, because the data that I had, the information that I had, that is something that I took note of just very shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you rely on any orders of any kind? Did you rely on any intercepted orders of any kind?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: All that is in my notes, all the orders I got hold of and all the information I could get hold of. So I always took notes about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So we can clarify this point, Brigadier, are we talking about personal notes that you made or are we talking about personal archives that you've kept?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, about personal notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I did not understand your answer.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What I said now, I said about personal notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you rely on any archival documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said all the documents that came into my hands, I took personal notes of that, so whatever went through the archives, whatever I put in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, after you took personal notes of these documents, what did you do with the documents? Did you send them to an archives?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I took notes during the whole wartime period in my diary, but later on, I did not go back to the archives because I already had everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Listen to my question very carefully, please, Brigadier. The documents from which you took your personal notes were sent to an archives; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What was done with those documents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said that all the documents that I had and all the estimates that I had made, I also kept a diary and made my own notes, an internal diary. And while I was preparing the notes for now, the ones that I told of you, I did not go back to the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You misunderstood my question, Brigadier. My question was, after you took a document and made a note from it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I wouldn't like us to go too far away from our goals here. What are you trying to achieve? What the Judges want to know is whether, through all the documents that were presented and commented on by the Defence witness, you consider that his evidence is relevant or not. Let us not make any mistakes on that, and please let us go forward, in as much as we can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, let me take the first visual aid, and I have one small question about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If we could have the assistance of the usher and, Mr. Dubuisson, if you could place the small number 1 on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, I just have one or two small questions about this particular visual aid that you assisted in the preparation of.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number D183/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you see that on your monitor, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The only question I have about this particular exhibit, Brigadier, you see the Vitez-Busovaca pocket and then the Kiseljak pocket depicted in pale yellow in an area surrounded by green?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What time period does that particular configuration of the two pockets come from? Which year, what month, if you're able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This state of affairs was valid already after the Washington Agreement was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. Now, if we could put 4B on the ELMO, Brigadier, do you see that on your monitor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in your testimony, you failed to give us a particular date. On the top of this diagram, it says that this is the organisational formation, and it indicates the 1st of December, 1992. Does this diagram, 4B, represent the structure of the 3rd Corps on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Just a moment. I must check in my notes. Yes, the 1st of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: As I understood your testimony, you prepared this based on your notes exclusively; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yesterday, you corrected this schematic, as I recall in your testimony, and you added four additional brigades, the 315th and 316th Brigades from Visoko, the 370th Brigade from Donji Vakuf, and the 311th Brigade from Kakanj, and those, you indicated, should fall under the area of mountain brigades, if I'm correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in your previous testimony, and I'm referring to the English transcript at page 11649, you indicated, Brigadier, that the 3rd Corps of the army -- I'm sorry, Counsel. I'm referring to lines 20 and 21. You indicated that the 3rd Corps of the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina was set up on the 1st of December, 1992. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, what was the date of the establishment of the corps in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The 3rd of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have the assistance of the usher, I would like to have the following exhibit marked as the next Prosecutor's order. For the record, Mr. President and Your Honours, this is an exhibit which has been translated only into English, and it is in the original BCS language.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document 467 and 467A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, do you see Prosecution Exhibit 467 in front of you? Do you see it in your language?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The decision that established the corps structures established those structures on the 18th of August, 1992; isn't that correct? If you turn to the last page, you'll see a date and, Colonel, you'll also see about that date, you'll see a sentence that reads that the decision shall enter into force on the day that it is issued?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The date is beneath the number, Sarajevo, the 11th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me correct you, sir. It's August the 18th of 1992; is it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes, on this exhibit of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At the bottom, it has, at least, a stamp of President Izetbegovic on the lower right-hand side of the last page; correct? Do you see the name "Ilija Izetbegovic" on that document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's examine that document together, Brigadier. I direct your attention to the first article of that document on the first page?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The first article establishes five corps, does it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, referring to the second article, and I'd like to direct your attention to 2nd Corps, second article, where it essentially identifies each of the municipalities where each of the corps will have authority; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The second article indicates the municipalities which were covered by the 2nd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And all five corps; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I won't name them all, but in 2nd Corps, there are approximately 20 municipalities or so, a large number of municipalities over which 3rd Corps had responsibility; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: You said the 2nd Corps covering 20 municipalities which were also covered by the 3rd Corps, so I didn't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I think there was a translation problem, Brigadier. Let me just get directly to the point. The municipalities, where each of the corps had responsibility, are identified in Article 2 of this particular decision; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I direct your attention to the 1st Corps area of responsibility, please. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is Fojnica municipality in the area of 1st Corps?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In this document, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And is Visoko also in the area of responsibility as defined in this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have the assistance of the usher, and if the usher would kindly place this map on the easel. Brigadier, would you kindly approach the map on the easel and take one of the coloured pens that's next to you, and would you please draw the boundaries of 3rd Corps as they existed on April 16th, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I have already shown you that boundary. The 3rd Corps, the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number of this document is 468.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you just take your --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's difficult with my tether to not block the diagram, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you hear what I'm saying, clearly?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You have drawn on with a red line going in a direction towards Croatia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The line --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: For the Judges, it's not very easy. The map is far away. The camera is doing what it can. Everyone is around the map. I would like to understand. Mr. Harmon, you want to ask the witness the boundaries of the command of the 3rd army corps. My question is to Mr. Harmon, are you doing it in relation to a document of a map produced by the witness? Is that the comparison you're making, because otherwise, I have to go up to the map. What is the comparison that you're trying to make? That is what I want to understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What I'm attempting to establish, Mr. President, first of all, this witness is an expert on 3rd Corps, he's testified about 3rd Corps, and I would like him to diagram the area where 3rd Corps had its geographic limits on the 16th of April, 1993, and that's my question and he has put a diagram for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier, there is no line between these two points. Can you draw the line where 3rd Corps had its geographic limits on April 16th?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. The line that I have drawn, you told me it was going to Croatia. That has nothing to do with Croatia. So if you saw my map, I draw it much better there, I should indicate the position of the Bosnian Serb army, then the positions of the HVO on this map, and then I should give you the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. I said that Gornji Vakuf and Visoko were included. This line went as far as the Bosnian Serb army, so I gave you the zone of responsibilities indicated with a line which, in military terminology, does not mark any limit. So forget the line. I'm just saying that I've indicated the left and right boundaries of the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question, Brigadier, is what is the southern boundary of the 3rd Corps which seems to be missing a line? Did it go down as far as Mostar?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. In my presentation, I said that it was the zone of responsibility which coincided with the zone of responsibility of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. And in military terms, this is how zones of responsibilities are indicated. But to give you a full idea of the deployment, I would need to draw in all the elements on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, I would like to be a little simpler than that. Where does the zone of responsibility for 3rd Corps end in this region? How far down did it go? Can you draw a line connecting these two points?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: If I were to link these two points, I would be missing the 4th Corps out, I would be leaving it out, and it was operating from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, wouldn't it be simpler to ask the witness, whether in relation to the decision of Mr. Izetbegovic, whether the south limits indicating the municipalities of the 3rd Corps, does it have a southern boundary, a southern limit in this document? Could the witness answer this question, otherwise, I shall have to get up and look at the map, and I'm not very knowledgeable about topography. I understand that you're going to call in question the credibility of the witness, but in the decision of Izetbegovic of the 18th of August, which of the municipalities, which are the furthest south. Perhaps that is not the best way of wording the question, but that's what I'm trying to put across.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may join in this discussion, I'm afraid that there may be an unintentional confusion by prompting the witness to give an erroneous answer, because Izetbegovic's decision is dated the 18th of August 1992, and my distinguished colleague is asking about the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps on the 16th of April, 1993, and this is a big difference because zones of responsibility change. So we have to be very careful as regards the date we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nobilo. We have to be very clear, Mr. Harmon. These are professional Judges. These games are accepted, but one has to be very clear. What exactly is your question regarding the 16th of April, '93? What do you wish to get from the witness so that the Judges could also understand what it is you're aiming at? And then the Judges will see whether this is in contradiction with what he has said or not. What is your question? Be very clear, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question, Mr. President, is on the 16th of April, can you please draw the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps of the Bosnian army?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. Fine. Is the witness going to do it? Are you capable of answering that or not, on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, yes, I am capable of doing it. I have indicated the left and right limits of the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. However, if I draw in the southern limit, which the Prosecutor is asking me to do, then that zone of responsibility enters into the zone of responsibility of the 4th Corps. I have indicated the northern boundary which links up with the other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, that is the answer. You have asked a question. Do you have another question to ask? You may not agree with the boundaries of the 4th Corps. If you have a question on the 4th Corps, put it, but the witness has answered your question. Do we agree?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm not interested, particularly, in the boundary of the 4th Corps. I'm interested in where the line on the southern part of this area of responsibility ended for the 3rd Corps, a very simple point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: But he told you that the southern boundary coincides with the 4th Corps of the army. Is that it, Brigadier? Either you wish to make maps of the overlapping, or you can proceed to another question, so please move forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I will yield at this point, Mr. President. I don't believe the witness is able to draw this line in. I yield.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Counsel can keep his comments to himself, please, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, quite. The word "yield" is not quite proper among professional Judges. The Judges are not asking you to yield. I never ask a party, nor do my colleagues ask for anyone to yield on a question. I'm just trying to organise the debate to make it more effective and clearer, so not yielding anything. If you have another question to put, go ahead. All I'm asking is that you shouldn't ask such complicated questions. Make them clear, and you will get clearer answers. I have to remind you that we are professionals. There's no place in trying to impress non-professional Judges, and, Mr. Hayman, thank you for your remark anyway. Let's proceed now, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will come back on one additional question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier Zeko, can you draw a line separating the area of responsibility from the 3rd Corps and the 4th Corps on that map?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That has already been done. The 4th Corps covered the area exclusive of Gornji Vakuf, not counting Gornji Vakuf, exclusive of Gornji Vakuf (indicating). This is the zone of responsibility of the 4th Corps, and over here is the zone of responsibility of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you mark it, please, for us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you, Brigadier. You can have a seat.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Usher, would you please place this back on the ELMO? Mr. Dubuisson, could the map be marked as a Prosecution Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, of course, 468.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I would like to direct your attention, Brigadier, to the various brigades that are listed under the mountain brigades. Let me ask you, directing your attention first to the first item, 302nd br.br.ZM Zenica. Are you aware that that particular brigade was located in the area of 1st Corps on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your diagram indicates that this particular brigade was based in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The 302nd Brigade is from Visoko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The 302nd Brigade is from Visoko. Is that what you're testifying to now?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So the schematic is in error where it says it's from Zenica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Was the brigade called the 302nd Mountain Brigade or was it called the 302nd Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Let me clear this up. All light and mountain brigades during the war developed into motorised brigades, and the light brigades developed into mountain brigades because of the personnel arriving in the territory. So that either other brigades had to be formed or because of their numerical strength, they developed into mountain brigades which numbered 1.800 men to 2.200 men. So that, depending on the availability of vehicles and other equipment, these brigades were transformed into motorised brigades, but I can't tell you exactly when each one of them were transferred into motorised brigades and when the light ones were transferred into mountain brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the fourth item down in that column, which is indicated as the 304th br.br.ZM Breza. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Could you repeat which one you're referring to, going down the line?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, I'm going down the lines of the fourth item, 304th Mountain Brigade Breza. Do you see that? I'm referring to the mountain brigades?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, was Breza located in the area of responsibility of 3rd Corps or 1st Corps on December 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, it's not very legible on some of the screens, so I would suggest that we provide the witness with the original documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: -- to read from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed. Let us try and speed up a little bit. Have you heard, Witness, it is the fourth yellow frame referring to the 304th Mountain Brigade of Breza. Can you see it now, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question was: On December the 1st, was that located in the 1st Corps area of responsibility or the 3rd Corps area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was under the 3rd Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I have a question for you. I want to know where we're going. Are you contesting the totality of this schematic or only some aspects of it? I think that we have to be clear in this debate. In that case, the Judges know that you are contesting the totality of this document. If I understood you well, first, you contested the source. You wanted to learn from the witness where these documents came from, and the witness gave you an answer. Now we're going to the next stage. We are not going to go at random like this, whether this brigade was there or not. My question is as follows: If you are contesting the totality of this scheme, on the basis of which document you are doing it? In other words, my question is: Are you contesting the totality of the document regarding certain minor contradictions, or do you believe that you have something to contest regarding the totality of the document? In that case, you should say, "I'm going to contest such and such a point and the totality." That is what I'm trying to say. You can do what you wish, but please, for God's sake, let's try and speed things up a little bit. Do you understand what I'm trying to say? Your duty is to tell the Judges, "I do not agree with such and such, Travnik, 312th Brigade," and that would be a clear question. Ask the witness regarding this particular brigade. Let's try and speed things up a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, so I can clarify for Your Honours, I contest a significant number of items that are described on this particular schematic. The witness has presented this as the organisation and formation of the 3rd Corps on the 1st of December, 1992. It is the Prosecutor's position that he is erroneous in a significant number of particulars, and I want to ask him about those particulars, one by one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I agree. But do you, yourself, have a document? If you have a document, it would be much clearer. You could provide a copy to the Judges. Does that mean that you don't have a document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't at the moment, Mr. President. I will have a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Then I'm telling you straight away that it's a pity, because today you have a document presented to the Judges that you, on the basis of your own sources, had another scheme to show the Judges, that would be much easier, but I'm not reproaching you, Mr. Harmon. It's not a reproach, but that would have been simpler. I would now like you to tell us, in summary form, on which points you're contesting this scheme on 1st December, '92? Is it the mountain brigades, the light brigades, Zenica, what is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will identify them for Your Honours, if you like, before I ask the witness the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The 304th Mountain Brigade in Breza, that is, item number 4, the 305th Mountain Brigade in Zenica which is five from the bottom; the 27th Krajina Brigade in Travnik, which is the last item; the 328th Brigade ZM Zavidovici, then I'm contesting, Mr. President, the schematic as it relates to the 303rd Light Brigade, the 323rd ZM in Kiseljak. On the right-hand side of the schematic, Mr. President, I'm contesting the artillery brigade, ZM Zenica. On the far right, on the top layer, the mixed POAD ZM in Zenica. I want to ask him a question to clarify the 7th Motorised Muslim Brigade which is a little bit lower on the right. Those are the items, Mr. President, that I would like to ask the witness specific questions about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well, but be very specific when you say you contest something, you must contest it either with a document, a written order, or evidence of any kind to indicate that you do not agree. Of course, this is your absolute right. So let's proceed. Let's begin.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I had asked you a question about the 304th Mountain Brigade in Breza. My question, sir, is was that unit located in the area of responsibility of 1st Corps or 3rd Corps in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, in order to assist the Prosecution, the whole schematic of organisation that I made is for the 1st of December, 1992, and it refers to the 3rd Corps. So all the units that I have shown, except for those units that were additional which are not here on the schematic, the four other ones that I mentioned, but whatever is on the schematic is under the responsibility of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention, sir, to the 305th Mountain Brigade which you indicate had a headquarters in Zenica. Now, are you aware that the headquarters of that particular brigade were located in Bijelo Selo which is near Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the 305th Brigade, it's a brigade from Jajce, which was formed from the refugees from Jajce, and it had commanding posts in Zenica, Kakanj, Travnik, and even in Bugojno. It did not have a permanent commanding post. Once they left here, I said they formed the brigade in Zenica. That's how I put it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My next question, Brigadier, is the last item in that column, the 27th -- I'm sorry, the Krajina Brigade ZM Travnik. Are you aware that that particular unit was not formed until October of 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Once the 1st and the 7th Krajina Brigade were joined, it was formed somewhere at the beginning of the summer. But up until then, it was called the Banja Luka Brigade. As I listed all the brigades by the number, I put the 27th Brigade, because previously it was called the Banja Luka Brigade, and it was commanded by Major Rasim Imamovic. While it was called the Banja Luka Brigade, it was at Mehurici, and after that, the command was in Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the 328th Brigade, Mountain Brigade in Zavidovici, are you aware that that brigade did not exist until 1995?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I know that it existed in this time period that I have shown here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention now to the column on the left, light brigades, and direct your attention first to the 303rd Light Brigade ZM in Zenica. Are you aware that that particular light brigade did not exist at all or are you thinking of another brigade by a different number?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, no, I think of the 303rd Brigade from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to the light brigade, the 323rd Light Brigade ZM Kiseljak. Was that in the area of 3rd Corps responsibility on the 1st of December or the area of 3rd Corps responsibility? I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Now, directing your attention to the artillery brigade, very quickly, which you will see on the schematic at this location. Do you see that, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it your testimony that that artillery brigade existed on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have the same question in respect of the mixed POAD ZM Zenica. Did that unit exist on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What do you think of? You mean the light anti-artillery corps, yes, it was from Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did that exist on the 1st of December, 1992?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. I'm satisfied with this line of questioning, Mr. President. Let me either pursue another line, or if the Court wishes to take a break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but before we take the break, I would like to draw the attention of both parties to what we've just seen here. Let us make a small summary. For the time being, the Judges have got a schematic which a priori is based only on the personal memories and notes made by the witness and maybe by informal sources that were not quoted here. In any case, the Prosecution had no access to them. On the other hand, we the Judges, we have a document which has not been disputed which comes from August 1992 and which gives the areas of responsibilities. I'm not speaking about brigades. I'm speaking about the geographical areas of responsibility which is an official document. I would like to invite the parties, if we take the decision from August 1992 and the schematic presented by the witness, which refers to the 1st of December, 1992, and if you don't seem to agree on that and if it seems that there are important differences, I would like to maybe invite the Prosecutor to present either maybe by writing memos or in writing in what way you contest the document. Because, for the time being, we have a witness who has a schematic and says there was a 3rd army corps which was very structured, and on the other hand, the Prosecution says we would like to dispute that on such and such a ground. Anyway, it is almost quarter past eleven, and we are now going to have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We will resume the hearing now. Please have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Let us proceed now. Mr. Harmon, you are cross-examining Brigadier Zeko.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier Zeko, in your testimony earlier, you testified at great length and gave us a number of statistics of the number of soldiers in each of those particular units on Exhibit 4B. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What did you base your calculations on?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I based them on all the gathered information and on the assessments.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you base your information on enrolment lists, captured enrolment lists, for example, of each of those units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On pay records for each of those units?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, when you testified about the numerical strength of those units, and I have reviewed your testimony, you did not tell us a date or an approximate date when those units had those particular strengths. Are you referring, in your testimony, to the numerical strengths of those units on December 1st, 1992, sometime in 1993, or sometime in 1994?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: During the whole period of the war, these strengths would vary. Depending whether there was a general mobilisation, then the number would be even larger than the one I gave. But after the mobilisation, obviously there were some people who were not capable to go, so they had to be excluded. So there were people who would not be enrolled in the units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So these numbers, essentially, commence on the 1st of December and are the numbers that reflect the strengths of the particular units on the 1st of December?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is leading the witness to give an erroneous answer. The witness has just answered that he couldn't give a particular date because the units would vary, the strength would vary, and he is not able to say that, on a particular day, the strength was of a particular number. So the Prosecutor tries to tell him whether it was on the 1st of December, and the witness has just answered that it was a fluctuating number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I've taken note of that. Mr. Harmon, would you like to answer or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I won't answer that. I'll go to another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you able, Brigadier, to give us an approximate number relating to each of these particular units in the 3rd Corps on the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, these are estimates you have given us. Can you tell us, please, what percentage of error you include in your estimates?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Five to ten per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you a question in respect of the 312th Brigade that you estimated had a strength of between 3.200 and 3.400 troops. Would it be consistent with your estimate, Brigadier, that in April of 1993, that particular unit had approximately 2.500 troops?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: First of all, I have to have a look at my notes to see whether the number is 3.300. The 17th Krajina Brigade, two brigades were joined, the 1st and the 7th, 3.300 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question is, Brigadier, in April of 1993, would it be reasonable, in your opinion, if I informed you that that particular unit, the 312th Brigade, had approximately 2.500 troops?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Between 2.200 and 2.300, I say roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention to the 306th Brigade where you testified that this particular brigade had between 2.100 and 2.200 men.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you aware that in April of 1993, that brigade had 1.320 men, approximately?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What do you have to say about that particular figure? Do you think it's too low, based on your estimate, or is it a reasonable figure, based on your estimate, and the percentage of error that you have told us are inherent in your figures?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Do you mean the number that you've just quoted?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. My estimate, I think it's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You testified also that the 17th Krajina Brigade had 3.300 men. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, we're contesting the numbers, and we'll be contesting the numbers that have been given by this witness, so if I can quickly go through a series of numbers with this witness, with the Court's indulgence, we will be able to later --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you are contesting the numbers, this is a question of method, so we shall not try and lose too much time. I think that you contest it because you have a number of elements at your disposal, and you have to indicate those elements. You have to present us documents, and the Judges will then make up their own minds once they see what the arguments of both sides are and their documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I intend to present the documents at a later time, I don't have them at my disposal at the moment, but I need to ask this witness first, to lay the foundation for those documents, whether the numbers that I'm going to be quoting are numbers that he would agree with or does not agree with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but if you bring the documents later on, that means that the Defence will always have to call the witness. How do you intend to proceed then? Otherwise, we'll have some difficulties. Anyway, we are not going to solve the question now, so please proceed. Let me just confer with my colleagues. Yes, please go on, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, you testified that the 17th Krajina Brigade had 3.300 men. My question to you is: In April, were you aware that they had only 900 men?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In April when?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: April of 1993, sir.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I know what I said. I gave the estimates. I was not claiming it was 3.300 men. I said it was around 3.300 men, and I said the probability to make a mistake is between five and ten per cent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would like to try and speed up our debate. On two or three occasions, the witness said that he is still maintaining the same figures with a five- or ten-per cent margin. I think that there are enough arguments for rebuttal, and I think that there's no point on going from one brigade to another when he says that he maintains these figures with a five- to ten-per cent margin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I grant this objection, but I will still ask the same question to the witness. Brigadier, do you maintain all your figures with a five- to ten-per cent margin of error?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In that case, Mr. Harmon, do you think that these figures, with a five- to ten-per cent error margin, for example, if there are really 3.300 soldiers in a particular brigade, which means that, to the maximum, it could be reduced by ten per cent, which means 330, 350 people, which will lower the figure to 2.900. If you're speaking of 900 soldiers in that particular brigade, are you basing it on a particular document? If you haven't got such a document, you will want to produce it later on -- if you haven't got a document, I was going to say it's your problem, but you claim -- just as well the witness is claiming it now -- and then the Judges will take a decision at an appropriate moment, or else maybe there are other possibilities. I think that the Tribunal, also the Trial Chamber, could receive written memos in that case instead of bringing the witness. I don't know. Anyway, please proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll move to another topic, Mr. President. This witness is standing by his figures, and the Prosecutor, in rebuttal, will present evidence to the contrary, and I think I can move on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, Brigadier: The units that you testified about and gave us figures about in the 3rd Corps area of responsibility, can you tell me, in April of 1993, were those units well-equipped or poorly equipped?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: My estimate is that they were well-equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I please have, Mr. Dubuisson, Exhibit 456/32, please? I'd like to show the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Brigadier Zeko, this is a special report that was prepared by your commander, Colonel Blaskic, on the 7th of May, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As I can see here, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, can you tell me, in respect of this particular communication, what type of communication this is, what form of communication this is? Is this a fax? Was this something that was sent by packet? Was this some other means of transmission of this particular report, if you're able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I can only say that this could have been sent either by fax or by packet. I don't know whether it was ever sent. This is the first time that I've seen this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This particular document was addressed to the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces of the Croatian community of Herceg-Bosna, the Head of the Defence Department and the Chief of the Main Headquarters. Do you see that in the addressee list?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If you turn to the last page of this particular document, Brigadier, do you recognise the signature of Colonel Blaskic on the last page?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this was a defence military secret and it was strictly confidential, as it appears on the upper right-hand corner of this document; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: These kind of strict military secrets were sent in coded form, were they not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They should have been sent in such a form or by messenger.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 7th of May, 1993, the pocket was surrounded, wasn't it, by the Armija?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, is it likely that this particular report was sent by courier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I cannot claim that. It could not have been sent by courier if it was a pocket.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention, if I can, please, to that portion of this special report that deals with Muslim forces. Do you see that portion I'm referring to? Since I can't read the language, I can only direct you. It may be Muslimanske Snage, which appears on the second page of the order in BCS. Perhaps Mr. Nobilo can help me if I'm correct in my language, Muslimanske Snage.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes. You've already learned Croatian. On the second page, it says Muslim forces, their strength, their composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you see that section I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you go to the second paragraph, please, the second paragraph under Muslim forces, where it says "Structure," and could you please tell us how Colonel Blaskic characterised whether or not the Muslim forces were well-equipped or how they were equipped?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What I can answer is that on the basis of the information that was gathered, which we sent out --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You didn't understand my question, Brigadier. My question is: How did Colonel Blaskic, on May the 7th, characterise the state of equipment that was available to the Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Well, the situation as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness did not see this document before, and he obviously does not know what he has to read. What I propose is that either my colleague read it or maybe I can read it out, and after that, the comments should be made, because obviously they cannot agree on what the witness has to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. I think that the question was not very well put. I suppose, Mr. Harmon, as this is a document signed by the accused Colonel Blaskic at the time, the estimate of the strength of the Muslim forces, you want the second paragraph starting with "Muslim forces." Do you agree with me that's the paragraph, which says "The structures are" --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In that case, I think it would be much simpler to ask you to simply turn to the witness and say: Under what Colonel Blaskic has signed, it seems that the Muslim forces were relatively poorly equipped. As for Mr. Nobilo, I've noted your observation, but I think that it is not too complex for the witness to answer on that particular point. But in case the witness needs a bit more time to read the document, we will give it to him, but I think that for the time being, it is not the case. Now I'm going to ask the question. On page 2, starting with "Muslim forces," can you find it in your document? I have got it in French. I've received it from the registrar. When it says, "Mostly infantry units were relatively poorly equipped." Is this your question, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What do you think of that, Mr. Nobilo? Maybe you want to make another comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Let me just add something to it. I'm afraid of asking such questions to people who have no experience in court because I insist that he should read the complete sentence. If we simply say that the units were poorly equipped, it is not enough. The witness has to read the whole, the whole sentence which gives the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I did not want to just leave out half of the sentence. I simply wanted to point out the sentence, which is not a very long one. Please, Brigadier, read this sentence which, in French, starts with "Structure:" In French, it's exactly four lines, and once you have finish reading, please tell us. I think that the interpreters do not have the text. In that case, I will read it: "Structure: Mostly infantry units, poorly equipped, essentially without military uniforms, dressed in civilian clothes only, the battalion commanders having complete uniforms, which explains why civilians are being killed. There are many," and so on. Everybody has read it. What do you think of it? This is your question, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, when you read the whole sentence, then you see what the assertion is, because I didn't make any assessment of the clothing worn. I just said they were equipped. Here it says with automatic weapons, snipers, and so on. So I stick to my assertion that they were, after all, well-equipped.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you then, Brigadier: What percentage of the men in the brigades, and you've given us a large number of numbers, had arms available to them, infantry arms available to them? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in respect of the Bosnian Serb army, was the Armija better equipped than the Bosnian Serb army or less well-equipped, in your assessment?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Less well-equipped. The army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was not equipped as well as the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, Brigadier Zeko, that the Armija in Central Bosnia and, in fact, throughout Bosnia, had no direct resupply lines, except those resupply lines that came through HVO-held territory?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question just once again?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. In 1993, did the Armija forces in Bosnia have any direct resupply lines, except through the territory held by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I don't know whether they had other supply lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could I have number 12 placed on the ELMO, please, Mr. Dubuisson, the small item showing the Serb confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, can you see that on your monitor, number 12?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does number 12 show the confrontation lines with the Serbs in the area of 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the Serbs, the Bosnian Serb army, was one that was extremely aggressive, was it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In fact, the Bosnian Serb army had conquered a fair amount of the territory in Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They were, in fact, continuing to press their operations in toward the area of 3rd Corps in 1993, were they not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At the beginning of the conflict between the Croats, those battles ceased. There was just the confrontation line between the Bosnian Serb army and the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In 1993, the Bosnian Serb army was continuing its murderous siege on Sarajevo, were they not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. I'm speaking about the 3rd Corps forces and the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. I'm referring to those units of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand, Brigadier. I broadened my question. At the same time in 1993, the Bosnian Serb army was attacking the enclaves of Zepa, Gorazde, Srebrenica, and other locations, posing a serious threat to the Bosnian Muslim population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You're aware, are you not, that in 1993, prior to April, a large number of the soldiers that were attached to the units which you have identified in Defence Exhibit 4A showing these various brigades, you're aware that a large number of those soldiers in each of those units held positions at front-line positions against the Serbs, did they not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: All those soldiers were not on the frontlines against the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you please tell us, Brigadier, using Exhibit 12, where the Bosnian Muslim forces were deployed along that front-line?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They are shown on this map --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, could the question be specified with a date? When? What period are we talking about when talking about the presence of the BH army on the front-line against the Serbs, because I think this is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask the question slightly differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the Bosnian Muslim forces along the front-line against the Bosnian Serb forces abandon those lines in April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They did not abandon those lines, but they just held the existing frontlines.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, Brigadier, in 1993, where the Bosnian Serbs attacked the front-line positions held by the Muslims in the 3rd Corps area of operation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Will you indicate the period, Mr. Harmon, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 1993, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, but at what point in time in 1993? Mr. Nobilo has just asked you that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Between April and June of 1993 would be my first question, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: There were no offensive operations by the Bosnian Serb army in that period. The frontlines were stagnant at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So if I understand your testimony correctly, the front-line position indicated on number 12, that's in front of you, there was no Bosnian Serb activity directed toward Muslim-held positions in the period of time that I've just indicated?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I don't understand now. You're asking a question about April 1993, and the map we have in front of us is dated May '92 to April 1993. We have to be very precise. Either we're referring to a map or we're not referring to a map. That is what I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You've asked a question about April to June '93, and you're asking the witness to answer with the help of a map which is dated for the period of May 1993. So will you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I understood the witness's testimony to say that these confrontation lines did not move at all in 1993 and, therefore, these confrontation lines are accurate representations of the whole year of 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you agree, Brigadier, with this?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In the period indicated, that is, until April 1993 -- 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In April of 1993 until the end of 1993, Brigadier, did the front-line positions between the Bosnian Serbs and the Bosnian Muslims move?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As far as I know, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You are unable to tell us where, from April of 1993 until the end of 1993, the units that you have identified in 4A were deployed along those lines; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That depended on the decisions of the corps commander. Parts of all units could have been engaged, but according to certain logic, parts of the 312th and the 306th may have been engaged with regard to the zone of responsibility facing the 1st Corps area of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did I understand your testimony yesterday, Brigadier, that 82.000 soldiers of the Armija came down and confronted the 8.200 soldiers in the pockets of Kiseljak pocket and the Busovaca-Vitez pocket?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I presented my assessment, that in the 3rd Corps zone of responsibility, the 3rd Corps had at its disposal this number of troops, and that the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia had the number of troops I indicated. They couldn't have all clashed at the same time. These were units that were being used in this area, and that was their numerical strength.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could we go to number 10, Mr. Dubuisson, of the small items?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, your commander, Colonel Blaskic, ordered that HVO forces attack Gomionica and Svinjarevo on the morning of the 18th of April. My question, sir, is: Does this particular exhibit, Exhibit 10, show the deployment of the attacking HVO forces against those particular objectives?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On this exhibit, what you are talking about, that is not shown, nor am I aware of this command that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would it surprise you to learn that Colonel Blaskic ordered an attack on Gomionica on the 17th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I can't answer that question, really.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You were the head of intelligence.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, but I wasn't in a position to know whether orders were written and where they were written.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I take it that you had no notes on that particular order when you prepared this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have Prosecutor's Exhibit 457/22 -- 456/22. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nobilo?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: I should like to draw attention to a point. This witness testified to the positions of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. In the examination-in-chief, this witness did not comment on the orders of General Blaskic, which he was not familiar with. But if we are limiting our questions to the examination-in-chief, we have no objections, but I think that this witness is not there to answer on the activities of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. Please do not go outside the examination-in-chief. This is in accordance with the Rules. Ask your question, and then we will see whether there is a reason to annul it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My only question relates to this particular exhibit that was tendered by the Defence that talks about the deployment of the forces from May through April of 1993. Unless I'm wrong, Mr. President, there is no showing of the deployment of the HVO forces at a time that is relevant for this particular schematic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: May 1992 or May 1993? The document is dated May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To April of 1993, according to the document that I have, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, quite. What is your question, so that we can see whether it fits within the scope of the direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you see the order in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you see that order at the time you were preparing this particular exhibit?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. No, I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The witness has answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no additional questions in respect of that exhibit. Let me turn to number 12, again, if I could have that placed on the ELMO, please? I'm sorry. Could we have this particular map placed on the easel?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Regarding this map, it is Exhibit 469.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you also have document 12 in front of you, which is this small diagram?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could the usher please furnish number 12 to the witness? Brigadier, number 12 shows the locations of two artillery positions where artillery could hit the town of Zenica. Would you please approach the map that is to your left, and would you please mark the site of those particular artillery positions around the Vlasic Plateau?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you kindly connect the artillery positions, which you've marked, with this location that is marked with a small red dot? Here's a pen. Draw a straight line between those two points.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: (Marks)

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, are you able to give a grid bearing on each of those lines?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness hasn't heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you able to give us a grid bearing on --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, no. I can't tell you what the grid reference points are. I've indicated the region of Humandzica Voda (phoen) and the region of Mejokrnje (phoen), the village of Zidzici (phoen). These were 155 calibre medium sized artillery pieces, and these are also medium sized weapons, which could have been positioned to the left or to the right, forward or backwards, and the positions I have indicated in Rakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the distance, if you're able to give us a rough distance, between this location and Zenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: For the record, could we have the location specified? It's not clear in the record which point Mr. Harmon is pointing to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm pointing to the lowest of the two lines connecting one artillery position to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the approximate distance?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Roughly 23 or 24 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm writing "23 to 24 kilometres" there. What is the approximate distance between the artillery position in the middle of the diagram going down to the Zenica location?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said to the area of Zenica municipality. I didn't say this particular spot. I said the municipality of Zenica. That is one thing. The distance is roughly 24 kilometres, 25, to the municipality of Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: For the record, I've written "24 to 25 kilometres" to the municipality of Zenica on this diagram. Two last questions: What type of artillery pieces, Brigadier, did the Serbs have at the location which I am marking with the letter "A"?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What type of artillery pieces did the Serbs have at the location that --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In the region of Bijelo Buce, 155 millimetre and 130 millimetre calibre. At this location, 155 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: At either location "A" or location "B" in April of 1993, did they have a 122-millimetre piece?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I do not have information that they had such pieces of 122 millimetres at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me ask you on another topic, Brigadier, how did the HVO, from April of 1993 until the end of the conflict, resupply itself with arms and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, objection. This is outside of the scope of the examination-in-chief, completely outside of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What were your intentions, Mr. Harmon, because it seems that this does go outside of the scope.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has testified that these two pockets were, essentially, hermetically sealed, and I wish to contest that. He has presented exhibits showing the Bosnian Muslim army surrounding the pockets for a considerable period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. All right. Continue with your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question, Brigadier, was, from April of 1993 until the end of the conflict, how did the HVO resupply itself with ammunition?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Somewhere in midsummer or up until the beginning of autumn, there were no supplies in 1993. Towards the beginning of autumn, it was done by air, by helicopters coming from Herzegovina. That is the way the supplies were brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Where was the Central Bosnia main supply base before April of 1993? Was it in Sebacic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. That was also at Grude, Posusje. Down there was the main centre of supply for Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the HVO resupply itself by ground, on the ground, over land, from its logistical base of support in Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, up until the beginning of the conflict. Later on, the roads were cut off, and I don't think there was any ground resupplying. I said at what time we started resupplying by air.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On the 26th of April, ammunition was in critical supply -- I'm sorry. The HVO was in critical need of ammunition in April of 1993 after the conflict had started; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am sorry to have to interrupt, but we're really now going into the details of what was the strength of ammunition on the 26th. I think this is completely outside of the scope and, in such a way, we are losing time. Very soon, we will call a witness who will speak about that, but if we ask all the questions to every witness, we will lose too much time. But we are going to call a witness that will speak precisely about those things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We've accepted the first question in as much as the witness gave us the position about the pockets in which the HVO found itself surrounded by the Bosnian army, but now I think that this is going too far, so the objection is granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I ask some questions in respect of the helicopter flights that the witness has identified?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No, no. I think that this is going to be tackled in a different form, because the Defence just told us about that. Have you finished, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I would now like to now ask the witness some additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Specifically, Brigadier, the HVO took over a number of JNA barracks in 1992, did they not? For example, let me give you some examples. Did the HVO take over the barracks at Slimena, and you may have to pardon my pronunciation, Slimena?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Slimena.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What area are you speaking of and what date? I do not understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a JNA barracks at Slimena in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Slimena, no, it's not a barracks. That was a warehouse of the Territorial Defence of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Did the HVO take over the JNA barracks at Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the HVO take over the JNA barracks in Busovaca known as the Draga barracks?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: The same objection. I'm sorry, Mr. President, but we are going outside of the scope of the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I've heard that, and I knew you would be saying so. I wanted, simply, that Mr. Harmon continues with his question. Just please put a straight question, Mr. Harmon. Do you think that you want to ask the witness whether these barracks were taken over by the HVO, so ask your question, and the witness will answer, but go straight into the question, and then we will see whether we will accept your question or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to identify for you, Brigadier, some other locations that I think the JNA took over, and I'd like you to just affirmatively say yes or no and then I'm going to ask you some questions about that. Did they take over the JNA barracks in Kiseljak?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: I think there was an error in the question, Mr. President. The JNA didn't need to take over the JNA barracks. The JNA had their own barracks. I think counsel meant the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well, I have been corrected. Thank you, kindly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, please don't answer instead of the witness. Let us bring some order into this. Mr. Harmon, what is your aim now with these questions? Are you trying to show that the HVO took over some barracks? What do you want to prove by that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this witness testified yesterday, first of all, about the seizure by the Armija of various critical facilities in Central Bosnia. Among those facilities were the facilities that dealt with production of weapons. They also took over additional facilities, which I'm trying to get this witness to acknowledge they did before I can get into a series of questions I'd like to ask him about those take-overs. I don't intend to belabour the point, but I need to establish, as a predicate, that the HVO took over these facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, and that is precisely what I am claiming is outside of the scope of the examination-in-chief. If my colleague had asked questions about the manufacturing of weapons and the factories that manufacture weapons, that would be all right, but he's speaking of a different thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I don't agree. I said to Mr. Harmon that his question was not direct enough. He explained to us what he was trying to pursue, and I think that this is completely consistent with the way he is working, and I think that he, as a Prosecutor, has the right to ask such a question. Let us now go back to it. Brigadier, have you understood? This is precisely what you mentioned yesterday when you spoke about the Bosnian army who wanted to get hold of some strategic facilities for its supplying. But did the HVO take over some of these facilities or not? Please let's go straight to the point. "Yes" or "no," did the HVO take over all these barracks? Now, just give a list. Don't ask a series of questions, just give a list, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The last location I was interested in asking him about was the JNA military barracks at Stojkovici?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I do not know that barracks. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will come back to that, because it may be a question of my pronunciation. Let me ask you then, Brigadier, at each of these locations that I have identified, did the HVO seize equipment that had belonged to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
