utterances.text: These facilities were taken over at the time when the HVO and the Armija were together, so they took them over together at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did they --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: But I cannot tell you about the equipment, who took how much from those facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you mentioned the TRZ facility in Travnik. Could you tell the Court, with a little more detail, what the TRZ facility was?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This was a technical maintenance institute where complete maintenance was done for all the command vehicles, all the signalling vehicles, and also for some other equipment for signalling, radios, the 33 up until the RU-515, 312, and the 12-K one and so on. Mainly, it was the signalling equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was communications equipment; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, for communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the HVO took that facility over, did they not? The Armija did not assist in the take-over of that facility, did they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At the same time, they were together, the TO and the HVO. They were together in the barracks for awhile, too. The technical and maintenance institute, the HVO never took over. The barracks and the maintenance institute are two separate facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did the HVO receive any of the communications equipment from that particular facility?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I have the following exhibit as the next Prosecution Exhibit in order?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked Exhibit 470 and 470A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, you have the document in front of you. Would you turn to the Croatian version of that document, and would you take a look at the signature on the last page of that document? Do you recognise that signature as belonging to Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, the date of this document is the 13th of October, 1992, if you look in the upper left-hand corner, and this document is directed to the commander of the Travnik municipal headquarters; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to the first paragraph of that. Could you read that to yourself? I would like to ask you some questions about that in just a moment. Read the first paragraph. Have you had time to read that document, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yesterday, you testified that the HVO did not receive a single vehicle from the TRZ factory in Travnik. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This particular document signed by Colonel Blaskic was directed to the commander of the Travnik municipal headquarters. Isn't that where you worked?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, this particular document, in the first paragraph, cites two decrees which, essentially, decree that all property of the former JNA on the territory of Herceg-Bosna are transferred to Herceg-Bosna, does it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. We can see it in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, was the TRZ factory that is referred to in this document on the territory of Herceg-Bosna?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I cannot give you a clear answer, whether it was or it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In fact, Brigadier, all of the property that was in that particular factory, the TRZ factory, as of the 13th of April, 1992, was under the control of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: On the 13th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I made a mistake, Brigadier. I meant the 13th of October.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. I don't remember this document. I've never seen this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Isn't this a document where Colonel Blaskic reprimands the commander of the Travnik municipal headquarters that materiel is being removed from HVO units?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, again, I think that this is a misleading question. The question was, doesn't this document show that materiel is taken from HVO units to the BH army, but once you have read the whole document, the title says the relations towards common property and property that was at TRZ --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You are going to speak about this, Mr. Nobilo, during your re-examination. Mr. Harmon, you can finish now on this particular point. Have you done so?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask one final question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, doesn't this document indicate that this communications equipment and materiel was in the possession of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Out of the title, we can see that this was joint property and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So when you testified yesterday that the HVO did not receive a single vehicle, you were mistaken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Brigadier, you can elaborate your answer. You can say more than either "yes" or "no." Maybe I did not hear you quite well. Was your answer "no"? The question was whether you made a mistake. You cannot, on the one hand, say that you either agree or do not agree with the Prosecutor, you have to give your answers, but if you say "no," you have to say why not. Mr. Harmon, I'm asking for your opinion. This document shows that the HVO received the materiel from the TRZ factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President. It also shows that some of that equipment was taken from HVO members, and that is the gravamen of the warning issued by Colonel Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: If we're going to argue, Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Just a moment. I'm going to pursue my question, because I cannot be satisfied with this answer. Mr. Harmon, what was your question to the witness? You asked him whether he made a mistake yesterday by saying the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's what I asked him, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is your answer, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, the answer is that the HVO did not receive any communications equipment from the TRZ factory, because we can see in this document that that was joint property, joint equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You have no other explanation to give?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, I don't, because I did not see any such equipment in our units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Because you did not personally see it. Now we have an objection by Mr. Hayman. Is your objection still valid now at this point?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Simply to point out, my learned friend has suggested that this document shows appropriation of property by the HVO. The items listed being complained were appropriated by the BH army, whereas they should have been left under joint control which, apparently, had been the agreement concerning these materials. I simply wanted to make that comment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I leave you the responsibility to give your own assessment. Have you finished on this particular point, Mr. Harmon? Have you got any other questions for the witness within the cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I do, Mr. President, but I see it's 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. We are going to have a recess now, and we will continue at 2.30. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.00 p.m. 24 25

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The hearing is resumed. Please have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Mr. President, Your Honours, and Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier Zeko, this morning when we were using the particular map and you drew the artillery positions, you drew a line from the respective artillery positions at points "A" and "B" to a location in Zenica. You testified in your examination when you gave a distance, that the distance you gave was to the Zenica municipality lines. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could you please take the blue pen that's in front of you to your right, and would you draw the Zenica municipality lines, to the best of your ability, where it intersects those two red lines?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The municipality of Zenica is a broad term. It includes many villages around the town, the whole territory of Zenica municipality. I said that the range went as far as Zenica municipality. I didn't mention the coordinates or the specific points you asked for.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I understand that. I understood your testimony this morning, Brigadier, to be that the distance that you gave was a distance not to the point which is at the bottom of the diagram, "X," but somewhere short of that point, that is, the municipality lines in Zenica. Did I misunderstand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, not the limits, but the territory of Zenica municipality. If you want me to indicate exactly the place in Zenica municipality, that is something I ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I didn't get a complete answer, "something I" and --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: You told me the borders of Zenica municipality. I told you the territory of Zenica municipality, the area which may be halfway into the municipality, a part of the municipality, certain locations within the municipality. I did not mention any specific coordinates as to the exact range.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll go to another area, Mr. President. Could I have the assistance of the usher, please? That would be the Prosecutor's next in order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 471, 471A for the French version, and 471B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right. First of all, let me direct your attention, Brigadier Zeko, to the one-page document that is in your language. Do you have that in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This appears to be an order from Colonel Blaskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what type of communication this was? Was this via a fax or was this via a packet or was this via some other kind of communication?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It may have been by fax or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you know where this document originated from, which municipality?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is marked "Defence Military Secret" in the upper right-hand corner; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, would you turn to paragraph number 9? Do you see your name in paragraph number 9?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you remember attending that particular meeting that was held at U.N. headquarters in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It is stated here at the U.N. base, not at the U.N. command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you remember attending that meeting?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I cannot remember, but probably I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Could I have the assistance of the usher in marking the next exhibit, please? Mr. President, this comes in French translation, with an English translation as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 472, 472A for the French version, 472B for the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you have a copy in your own language in front of you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a report that was issued on the 30th of January, 1993 at 2015 hours, and it was addressed to Colonel Blaskic in Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is marked "Defence Military Secret Strictly Confidential" on the right-hand side; do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what type of communication this was? Was this by a fax? Was this by another system of communication, or are you able to tell?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. It could have been any type of communication, by fax or something else, but what it was exactly, I can't tell you because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in January 1993, there was fighting in Busovaca, was there not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This message was sent from the Vitez forward command post to Kiseljak; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: First of all, where was the Vitez forward command post?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In the Vitez Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, Brigadier, this defence military secret that was strictly confidential, was this encrypted when it was sent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It need not necessarily have been encrypted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So there were some times when you didn't encrypt military secrets that passed through hostile territory; is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, because this document, I didn't send it, nor can I claim what method was used in sending the document, how it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Having seen this document, do you remember the document? Do you remember the meeting at all?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you one question in respect of this particular document. Do you recognise the signature at the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Whose signature is that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The chief of staff of the headquarters, Franjo Nakic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That particular meeting, as you recall, dealt with the events that were occurring in and around Busovaca, did it not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The people who attended that meeting are identified on the first page of that document. They include Mr. Stewart, Mr. Flemming, and other representatives described on the first page?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Harmon, can we speed up a little bit with your questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm finished with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: There's no point in asking the witness whether the names of the participants are indicated. We can all see that. Please proceed to the question that you're targeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I've concluded with that particular document, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: While counsel is finding his next document, Mr. President, I would just like to put on the record the position of the Defence, that this is a document, Exhibit 472, we've never been given before, and it is exculpatory in two respects. One, in it, the chief of staff of the HVO is recommending that the HVO urgently seek a cease-fire, even though, in the prior six days, the HVO had lost a very large and strategic swath of territory. Secondly, this document indicates that Colonel Blaskic was not at these negotiations because he was cut-off in the Kiseljak enclave, as the Defence has been suggesting to this Court for some time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm more than happy to address the issue of whether this document is exculpatory. I would rather do that at a later time, rather than take up the time of the Court. I will prepare and proceed with my next exhibit, if I can, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Continue. Mr. Hayman's observations have been entered in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would like now, Brigadier, to go over some of the exhibits that you identified yesterday, Defence Exhibits, and I would like to start with Exhibit 185. I'd like to direct your attention, please, to the first paragraph with the number 1 in front of it and recall your testimony from yesterday, Brigadier. Brigadier, yesterday you testified that this particular document was, and I quote -- I'm sorry. You characterised this particular document, and I don't have a page reference, that the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which, at that time, was the Territorial Defence, was to continue collecting information about the HVO which has already called aggressors and to commit their units to reinforce action. My question to you, based on the English translation that I have received from the Defence, refers to the units of the HVO, in the first paragraph, and activities of the aggressor. It seems to make a separation between the aggressor and units of the HVO. Do you see that in your document at the end of paragraph 1?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I see it, but the HVO is being placed together with the aggressor, because information is being collected about both.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I see. I just wanted to clarify that point. The aggressor in 185 refers to the Serbs, not to the HVO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said exactly as it says: "Collecting information about the activities of the aggressor and the activities of the HVO," which means both, and it means placing them on a footing of equality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's not exactly how you testified yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let me turn, if I could, to 186. Mr. Dubuisson, if you could make that exhibit available to the Brigadier, I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you tell me, please, what, in your opinion, this particular document represents?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It represents a memo of one of the commanders, in this case, Enes Varupa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In what time period does this document relate?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The first date that appears is the 17th of February, 1992 until it reached me, until the document was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: There's also another date on this document of April 11th, 1992, is there not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, to put this into context, in April of 1992, could you tell me what the Bosnian Serbs were doing in respect of attacks on the Busovaca, Vitez, and Kiseljak municipalities?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In that time period, mostly artillery actions were engaged in and air raids, air attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: They were waging war against the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims in Central Bosnia, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It was imperative, was it not, that both the Bosnian Croats and the Bosnian Muslims organise themselves to resist the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you testified about page 5 of that document. I'm sorry, Brigadier. I don't have a document that is paginated, but I can tell you the page I'm referring to is the page that starts with "Preocica," and it then lists a series of numbers next to the various locales, Bukve, Bila Ceta, Kruscica. Do you see what counsel, yesterday, referred to as page 5?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Is it the list ending with "Sivrino Selo"? Perhaps we could put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That might be helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: It would be clearer. We must bear in mind that the hearings are being held in public. Thank you, Mr. Hayman.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this particular page, you testified yesterday, was the number of soldiers that were located in these particular locations. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I would like to turn your attention to one of the pages that was not translated, nor presented to the Court, and it is the page, Brigadier, that has the caption of "Bukve" on the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Two pages later, I think. Am I right? After the one we've seen, there are two more, and then we come to this one; is that right? No, one more, actually. Am I right, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this was not given to me in any particular order, so I'm having some difficulty in organising this. I can only identify by the name at the top of the page which page I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I see. Mr. Hayman is coming to the help of the Prosecution, the page beginning with "Bukve" and ending with "Veceriska"; is that the one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, does this particular page identify the type of weapons and equipment that are available in Bukve?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is just a part of the vehicles and means available.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is there another part of this document that describes other weapons and other vehicles that are available in Bukve?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I do not have any other part of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Fine. Then I'm limiting my questions to this particular page, Brigadier. Would you please read the kind of weapons that are available in Bukve?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Two semi-automatic rifles; 18 or 12, it's hard to read, shotguns; 14 pistols, 15, whether this is autos or automatic rifles, I don't know. Then, one freight vehicle, two tam trucks, five tractors, two carts, five horses and motorcycles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me turn your attention then to Sadovace, the page that lists the equipment available in Sadovace?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Sadovace?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please tell the Court what kind of weapons and equipment are available in Sadovace, according to this particular document that has been entered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. According to this document, there were eight pistols, three hunting rifles, a radio transmitter, RM without the number being indicated, six automobiles, and one semi-automatic rifle, passenger vehicles, 15; freight vehicle, one; tractors, four; carts, two; and motorcycles, one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, again, the village of Gacice appears on the top of one of these pages from this diary. Tell the Court what kind of weapons were available in Gacice and what kind of equipment was available in Gacice?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I'll read from the document. One machine gun, RSRM, which means a radio transmitter, an automatic pistol, one; three semi-automatic rifles, six carbines, eight hunting rifles, ten pistols. Those are the weapons. Among the vehicles, there are three tractors, six horses with three carts, and then automobiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see the page that says "Divjak"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Describe the equipment that was available in Divjak, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I just have a list here of the villages, Muratovici, Bukve, Sadovace, Bila, Grbavica. Perhaps I haven't got the right page. There's no list of equipment here at Divjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On my page, Brigadier, it appears next to "Donje Veceriska" as well?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. Divjak: 34 men, two automatic rifles with a radio transmitter, four hunting rifles, eight pistols, ten automobiles, one tam, five freight vehicles, one tractor, a motorcycle, and a cart.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Lastly, Brigadier, could you read the equipment that was available in Donje Veceriska?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Donje Veceriska: A platoon of 40 men, two automatic rifles, one machine gun, one carbine, ten pistols, ten passenger cars, one FAP, six tractors, one or two carts, and a motorcycle. That's all. And ammunition, which the quantity is not indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In April of 1992, Brigadier, in the face of serious Bosnian Serb aggression, was this equipment unreasonable to possess by the villagers of those villages that you have just identified?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: These places here, all these locations that were indicated here were not interconnected, and they were not near the position of the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So are you saying, Brigadier, that if you weren't near the confrontation lines of the Bosnian Serbs, then you shouldn't have armed yourself in the face of what was happening to Sarajevo, what was happening to the enclaves, what had happened at Vukovar, that it was not appropriate to arm yourselves?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, no. That is not what I mean. But they were arming themselves just as much as they could, depending on their possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In April of 1992, against whom were they arming themselves?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Against the aggressor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The common aggressor was the army of Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, if we could turn to Exhibit 187, this is a document, Brigadier, that has been entered into evidence, and you have identified the person who sent this document as Zeljko Katava. Let me ask you some questions about this particular document. This document was sent on the 6th of January, 1993 from Busovaca, and it was a defence military secret marked confidential; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, the answer is really obvious. Please speed up, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To whom was this document sent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: From the heading, we can see that it was sent to the command, ZSV, Central Bosnia, to the head of the Military Intelligence Department.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who requested that this particular document -- who ordered that this particular evaluation be made?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Here, the request was made by the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is this a request that was made by Colonel Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I don't remember whether it was made by Colonel Blaskic or by the head of the chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yesterday, you characterised this particular document as representing the intentions, and I'm quoting, "the intentions of the Bosnian army." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Which intentions does this document reflect?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The intentions which came through later on. We can see it in the document. This is a document that I had received, and it was used, the evaluation, as the estimate for the whole Operative Zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this document was prepared about two and a half weeks before the conflict in Busovaca between the HVO and the Armija; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you tell us earlier today that before offensive operations were prepared, intelligence assessments were made of objectives of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, the witness has said just the contrary. Counsel for the Prosecution is trying to put words in the witness's mouth which he did not say. He answered this question that he had forwarded routine reports to the commander, regardless of the fact whether the commander planned any combat activities or not. This question was asked several times, and the answer was always the same. Now, in his question, the Prosecutor is saying to the witness that he had stated that he gathered this information, which was not said by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Please reformulate your question, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In the HVO, Brigadier, before an attack was made by forces of the HVO, was there an assessment made of the objective of the attack, specifically, identifying the forces, their locations, their strengths, the type of weapons that they had?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The HVO had mounted defensive operational combat activities, and for that kind of combat activities, assessments were also made, which is normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Not only defensive, but offensive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: He told you defensive, Mr. Harmon. Don't try to make the witness say what he did not say, otherwise ask your question a different way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: His answer, according to my translation, has the word "also made," implying they were made for defensive purposes, as well as offensive purposes. That's why I tried to clarify that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So, let me, just to clarify that point, Brigadier, you said these kind of assessments were made for defensive operations; were these kind of intelligence assessments made by the HVO for offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I said for defensive operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that mean that these kind of assessments were not made for offensive operations?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: HVO had defensive operations in the Operational Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you answer my question, Brigadier? Were these kind of intelligence assessments made for offensive operations by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: He answered your question, Mr. Harmon. He does not want to say that there were offensive operations. This answer certainly is not convenient for you, but we cannot do anything, because he doesn't want to say that there were any offensive actions. You can't go any further than that. If you want to show that there were offensive operations, in that case, you will do it in the manner that will be appropriate. But now we have to remain more into our subject, and I will turn now to the witness, and I will ask the witness to answer in a more precise way to the questions. Mr. Harmon, ask very precise questions and then the witness will answer very precisely and the Judges will not have to intervene.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, on September the 8th, 1993 did the HVO conduct an offensive operation at Stari Bila, at the hill at Grbavica?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that action was carried out with the purpose of stopping further advancements towards SPS.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you prepare intelligence assessment before that operation was conducted?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That assessment had already existed from before. It was known how much personnel and holdings existed in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you to look at this particular document and turn to the 4th paragraph in this document, please. Do you see in the middle of that particular paragraph the sentence that reads, quote, "Until now they have been dispatching 160 soldiers to the battlefields in Visoko Turbe"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Visoko and Turbe were front-line positions against the Bosnian and Serb aggressors; correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to the line that reads as follows: "We have unconfirmed information that they suffer from a deficit of ammunition and shells for artillery pieces."

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention further to a line to where it says, "Nowadays they are dispatching soldiers to the Maglaj battlefield, about 160 of them." That is, that appears, Brigadier, underneath the previous sentence I read about Visoko and Turbe.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who was fighting at Maglaj battlefield?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Both the HVO and the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to a sentence on the English version that reads as follows: "So far Muslim forces have not undertaken any concrete action except patrolling their sectors."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It might go faster if we tell the witness where in this 3-page document that sentence can be found, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I agree, but I can't read the language, and I'm trying to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's toward the end, Brigadier, in my English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: In the English version it is on the top of page 3. Is that it, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In my text it says, "According to unverified information they received, in part, Howitzers, then 128 millimetres, and according to unverified information they do not have enough ammunition for artillery." Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, two paragraphs down, Brigadier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm prepared to let the document speak for itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think this is very easy. It's very easy for the witness. It's about the last third of the document underneath the name Miro Zermin. I cannot read this in your language, but underneath Miro Zermin, this name, but this is in English. So far and so on. So, if I can find it, I think it can certainly be found by the person who reads the language. Brigadier, please.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: If I found it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, it's "So far," yes.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. "So far Muslim forces have not, except by patrolling in their sector, undertaken anything more concrete."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Your question, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So this is a document, in your opinion, that shows the aggressive intentions of the Bosnian Muslims on January the 6th in Busovaca. That's your assessment of it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This is the evaluation of the assistant of the chief of the intelligence, military intelligence department in Busovaca, which I have received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, could I turn to document 190, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to direct your attention to a portion that is three paragraphs, two paragraphs from the bottom of this document. Two paragraphs from the end of this document. It starts with the word "Observing and analysing the activities." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: What territory do you mean? What area? First page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The last two paragraphs from the end of this document. There is the signature line, two paragraphs from the end.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: "Observing and analysing the activities undertaken up to now."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday you testified that the Muslims were utilising the tactics of the aggressor, that's what this particular report says. And those tactics consisted of four elements; the capture of territory; the regulation of positions; the moving out of the Croat inhabitants; and taking full control. Do you see that, in that particular report?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. If I read this well, "Observing and analysing the activities that were undertaken up to now, the potential aggressor --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, Brigadier, we have seen it. Ask your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The question I have --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: They are changing, they are applying the tactics. I did not say that they had applied the tactics, I said they are applying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you, when you say regulate positions; what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: How do you mean? I don't know in which, what is the meaning of this word that was put in here? So, I cannot explain. I need the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The context is the report that you wrote.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. But what text? In order to find the sentence that I can fully read it, and only then I can give it to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The second sentence in that paragraph that reads as follows: "He is occupying the territory part by part then regularising the situation in these areas, displacing the Croatian population and taking full control." That's the English translation of that document that has been provided to me. Do you see that sentence, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I see it. But in my text I will read the whole sentence: "With this activity they are taking part after part of that territory, and after that they regulate the positions, they move out the Croatian population and take complete control of" this is regulating the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My question is; what does regulating the positions mean?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: That's the regulation by engineers around the territories. It means fortifying, digging trenches, organising the whole firing system on those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, those tactics were tactics that were used by the army of the Republika Srpska, the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In Ahmici on the 16th of April, did the HVO capture the village of Ahmici?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is outside of the scope of the case in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Please reformulate your question, or otherwise change your question, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have a copy of the transcript in which this witness testified precisely to what I'm asking him. It is clearly within the confines of the examination. He has testified and he has -- I do not have a page quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Would you make your question more precise? How come that from a question you're asking where you're simply asking what regulating the position means; and then you start from a very far away question, and that is the problem of such type of questions. We never know where you want to get with those questions. I'm saying to you today, and tomorrow I will say to the Defence; how do you want to get to Ahmici? What is your real purpose? What do you want to ask the witness? Just ask this question very directly. Your preceding question was: What does it mean to regulate the position? So, what is your next question, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: My next question, Mr. President, is this:

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, were these very same tactics used in the village of Ahmici by the HVO on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I have understood, and unfortunately you did not need to ask this question for the moment. Please ask a different question. You cannot ask this witness what were the tactics used by the HVO. The whole Blaskic case is turning around this question, mostly; so, we cannot now try, in explicit terms, regulating the position, so I cannot accept this question. Ask another question. Please speed up. You cannot isolate sentences from the document just like that. Otherwise, you have a specific plan, Mr. Harmon, but continue with your plan; but please be more direct in your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll move on, I can't be any more direct than I was, but the Court -- I will move to a different question. If I can have 192, please, placed before the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this document was issued six days before the attack on Ahmici, and it is a report from the Vitez brigade command. To whom was it sent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was sent to the commander of the Vitez brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this particular document, in the second, sorry, the third paragraph, indicates that the soldiers from the 325th Mountain Brigade were being sent to the Serb frontlines at Visoko and Turbe.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: May I read the sentence? "In the area of Vitez municipality, the 325th Mountain Brigade was formed whose members were going through practical military training at the battlefield in Visoko and Turbe, where a part of the manpower is being engaged."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is a document that Colonel Blaskic was aware of, because yesterday you testified he received a copy of this document.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It may have been a misinterpretation. I didn't say that he got a copy, but I said that my department made an overall estimate, and he received the parts of reports which contained a part of this assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So, Colonel Blaskic was aware that ABiH units were sending their members to and rotating their members to and from the front-line positions against the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we go to document 193, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have one question for you, Brigadier, in respect to this document. The date indicates the 14th of March 1993, and yesterday you corrected this to be the 14th of April. There appears to be some hand-written correction done by some unknown party in that document. How do you know this document was issued on the 14th of April, as opposed to the 14th of March, 1993? What's your basis for stating that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The contents of the document, and because this was typewritten, and then we see that the number 3 has been crossed out with a typewriter and changed to 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is the content of the document that makes you believe this document was issued on the 14th of April as opposed to the 14th of March? What's the context of it?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It's a regular report about development in the zone of responsibility, zone of intelligence responsibility of this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is there anything else in this document, the content of this document, Brigadier, that you can assist me and assist the Court in understanding why you have concluded this document was issued on the 14th of April as opposed to the 14th of March? Can you be more precise?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The text says, and the date is what it is, unless you want me to read the text.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: You're not answering the question, Brigadier. You, yourself, said that the 14th of April, that you deduced that from the context; and the Prosecutor is asking you about that context on the basis of which you conclude that it is April. So, I'm taking you back to your own logic; agreed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I didn't quite understand the question. What is the question now regarding what I said?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Listen. I'm going to try and summarise. This afternoon seems to be rather complicated for everyone, perhaps because of the fine weather in The Hague, but it's very simple. The Prosecutor is asking you about the date. You, yourself, said it was the 14th of April, not the 14th of March. He asked you why, and you answered, among other things, that you are concluding that it is the 14th of April from the content of the document. And he is asking you what is the content, what is it that makes you say in view of the whole text that it was the 14th of April and not the 14th of March? So, please answer this question.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, it is the 14th of April on the basis of data that was collected at the time by the assistant in the brigade, in the Busovaca brigade, and which he sent to his commander and to me as the chief of the department for the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think you haven't answered the question. It is not up to me to ask you questions, it is up to the Prosecutor. Please go on to your next question, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If I could have document 194 placed in front of Brigadier Zeko, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, I would like to direct your attention to this particular document, paragraph number 4, it appears on the first page, and I would like to direct your attention, please, to the second line about which you testified yesterday. You see the second line, the date of that particular order, 02-33-867? What's the date on that second line in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As far as I can see on this document, the date is the 15th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I approach the easel, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. We are having a lot of discussion over dates and I'm rather like the Brigadier. My impression is that in the Serbo Croat version it is the 15th of April, Mr. Harmon. I don't know whether that's very important for you, but it is my impression that it is the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is it your conclusion from this document Brigadier Zeko -- what is your conclusion from this document, there is the date of the 15th of April, 1993? What's your conclusion? What is your conclusion from this particular date of the 15th of -- try again. Can you hear me, Brigadier Zeko?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I can hardly hear you. No. Yes, yes, yes, I've got it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What is your conclusion from the date that appears in paragraph 4, being the 15th of April, 1993. What's the significance of that date to you?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The date that the order was issued, means the preparations of the corps, instructions given to this brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What instructions were given on the 15th of April?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I could read the order to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Please, you don't have to read the order to me. Yesterday you testified that the date of the 15th of April 1993, on this document, was significant. And my question to you is very simple. What is the significance of that date, the 15th of April, appearing on that particular document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Preparations for the execution of combat operations on the part of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and giving instructions to this particular brigade, the 303rd. No, the 333rd.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me invite your attention and the Court's attention, please, to certain features on this document. And Brigadier, I'm going to ask you to look at this document very carefully for me. I'm going to specifically ask you to look at the characters that appear on this document. And you see this orange line that I've drawn right here? This orange line represents the bottom line underneath each sentence, it's not visible, but there is a certain horizontal plane. And let me direct your attention, please, to certain numbers that appear on this document. If you go down three sentences below the date we've been talking about, in the middle of the page you'll see the numbers "587." Do you see these particular numbers?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: 587, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I think in the English version it's "567."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It may be in the English version, but I'm referring, Mr. President, to the Croatian version.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the way those figures are formed, Brigadier, and then I want your analysis. Brigadier, will you look at these figures, please, very carefully, and just to help you in looking at these letters, I direct your attention, as well, to the second page of this document, and you'll see the numbers "567" in paragraph 5, the fifth line down?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me ask you to, please, examine the way these numbers appear on this page. Directing your attention to the numbers that I have previously directed your attention to, do you see how the number 5 goes below the horizontal base of the sentence? Do you see what I mean? I'm referring to this area right here, where the number 5 appears here, and the number 7 that appears to dip below. Could you examine the document, please? Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Can you explain what you're trying to show, please, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm asking the witness if the numbers, such as "5" and "7," are longer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: On the first page?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: On any page, any "5," any number "7."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Number 5, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And number 7?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Number 7, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: If they appear to go below the bottom line of the sentence, the invisible line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: If you prefer, if you take the dash as being the line, as being the base of the word.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The base of the word, Mr. President, and the base of the numbers appears to be ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you see what I'm talking about, Brigadier?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may be of assistance, my learned friend is asking the witness, who is not an expert, to provide expertise on numbers, and I think that that is inappropriate. On the other hand, if, in addition to number 957, then you see the next number, 921, you will see differences between the two 9s. Obviously, there are capital and small letters, because it is an old typewriter. But this witness is not an expert witness who could answer this question, so he's being asked to analyse something he is not familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Nobilo, I'm not at all in agreement with you. For the moment, Mr. Harmon has not asked him to provide expert opinion on typewritten numbers. Mr. Harmon, if I understand him well, is simply asking the witness, your witness, to note that there is a disparity between the numbers. Perhaps, Mr. Nobilo, you can justify this with an old typewriter and so on, but that is another problem. For the moment, I don't think we should interrupt Mr. Harmon. Please go on. You want to have this difference in the numbers stated, don't you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you see the differences I'm talking about in terms of the serifs of these particular numbers being below the plane on which these other numbers sit?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to two other numbers in this document, the date on the upper left-hand corner that says "16/4/93"; do you see that? Do you see the number 6?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does the number 6 appear, to you, to go below this line?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Not quite the way you've drawn it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does the number 6 in the date that appears "16/4/93," paragraph 3, appear to be one of these elongated letters like the numbers 9, 5, and 7?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. Number 6 cannot be elongated when it's quite a different number. It's turned the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to paragraph 4, which has a date that you said is 15. Let me ask you, where you say the 5 is, does there appear to be any elongation under the number which you say is 5?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This number 5 has no elongation, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In your opinion, Brigadier, is it more likely that that is number 6, similar to the number 6 that appears in "16/4/93" in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have come to what I said just three minutes ago. This is an expert opinion that is being asked, and it is appropriate to address such a question to an expert.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. I'm afraid I would be prone to agree with Mr. Nobilo. We are entering an area which is rather complex. You are asking someone who, a priori or a postiori, did not draft the document. You're asking him to note the differences between the numbers. Let's go to the end of your thoughts. Are you thinking that these may be forgeries? We can't stop halfway. I think things should be said to the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I wish to remind you that we need to have a break shortly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Perhaps now, Mr. President, would be an appropriate time to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do you have many more questions for your cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, I do not. I have some additional questions on this topic, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Yes. My colleague is reminding you that I asked you to go to the end of your thought regarding these numbers. Do you think that this document was, in some way, interfered with? What is it that you want to say? We can't stop there with this pseudo-expertise of handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness about another document, similar, and ask him for his opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Very well. I think that the interpreters must be tired. We're all lost in these figures. All I know is that it's five to four. It is a real four and a real five, and we're going to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We are now resuming. Please have the accused brought in. (The accused entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'd like to introduce the following exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'm offering Prosecutor's next exhibit, and this is an exhibit which is a better copy of Defence Exhibit 194.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would you like me to give it a new number with the number of a Prosecution Exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: So the document will be marked Prosecution Exhibit 474.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, what are you trying to show to us now about these figures?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I just want to introduce a better copy of Defence Exhibit 194. This happens to be a slightly clearer copy, and my intention is only to direct the Court's attention and the witness's attention to the number that has been in issue for the last few minutes, and that is whether, in paragraph 4, the second line, the date, it is; a "15" or a "16."

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, do you have Prosecution Exhibit 474 in front of you, and can you please take a look at the number and give us your interpretation of that number, now that this document appears to be a little bit better copy. Does that appear to be a "15" or a "16" in paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: As far as I can see, it is the same number that I have seen previously, which is "15." That is what I can see on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I would just direct your attention to the order number and the date that is found in paragraph 3 and the order number and date that appears in paragraph 4, just merely for your comparison purposes only. If I could have the next exhibit marked in evidence, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, I have to say, for quite awhile I've been wanting to say that maybe we can do it by referring to the number of the order. I suppose that the orders had numbers, and so different orders do not have the same numbers. In order to find out whether it is 15 or 16, in trying to figure out what it was, maybe we can see which order it was. There might be a slight imprecision, but in that case, that could help us. What do you want to say, Mr. Hayman?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We could really cut through this, Mr. President, if the BH government would give us the order of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have it, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We have asked them for it, and they told us they couldn't find it. Now, if the Prosecutor has had better luck at getting it, first of all, I would suggest it may contain exculpatory evidence, and he may have an obligation to give it to the Defence. Secondly, he might produce it, the BH government having declined to produce it to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, this is a public hearing, and I have to say that I fully agree with what you've just said, but I have to add that it would also help us if Croatia also answered to various injunctions that are issued when we ask for it. We have to count here on the cooperation of different states, and that is true. If the parties, both your party and the Prosecution, have at their disposal, all the various governments on which this depends, we should not have to go through this type of acrobatic accounting, trying to see whether this is a 5 or a 6. I agree with you, but I wanted to complete it. Putting this aside, I would like to ask the Prosecutor to ask the questions to the witness and try to find what number of the order it was, starting with "02." Please ask your question now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier Zeko, can you tell me what you believe the order number in paragraph 4 is, starting with "02-33"?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The number "02-33-867," that is the number of the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does that appear to be the same number that appears in paragraph 3?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Which number do you mean, number 8 or number 6?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: In paragraph number 3 of this document, there appears to be an order number starting with "02-33," and that is at the end of the second sentence. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: What number does that appear to be?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: "O2-33," and then the number that's here before. Only to my assessment, I think my assessment is that it should be "867."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: What is your aim now, Mr. Harmon, before we take a decision to try and find a way out of it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have one more question of this particular witness on Prosecution Exhibit 474, and then I will move to the order number 02-33-867, the Prosecutor's next exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Are you trying to prove that it was on the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. The Defence, yesterday, said that this document, their 194, said it was the 15th of April, and I am attempting to establish that the document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: No. The document is dated, the document itself -- just a moment. Which document are you speaking of?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. President, the Defence offered Defence Exhibit 194. They referred to paragraph 4, and they said that the date that appeared in paragraph 4 was the 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The 15th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can direct the Court's attention to the portion of the transcript, and I am attempting to establish that this is not the 15th, but the 16th of April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you. So now I would like to consult with my colleagues before giving our opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: The Judges have decided, in function of Article 98, we ask the Prosecutor to make the request to Bosnia-Herzegovina to give us the original of this order. And the motivation for it is that the Prosecutor has the interests to show that the order, 02-33-867, is dated the 16th and not the 15th of April. Mr. Prosecutor, this is the decision of the Trial Chamber, and please transmit it to the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We would like to have the original in our archives, the original of this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, there is no problem. I will convey that, Mr. President, as soon as I conclude with the court session today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Two last questions about 194A, the document we have been talking about. Do you have that in front of you, Brigadier, this order for attack of the 16th of April, 1993?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And the first paragraph I would like to direct your attention to, the order for the attack indicates why there is an order for this particular attack; does it not? It indicates that the HVO are committing brutal aggression in the wide area of Central Bosnia, focusing on Vitez, and especially in the direction of Ahmici. It goes on to say that the soldiers of the HVO are terrorising the civilian population. And it concludes by saying, does it not, that the basic goal of this aggression is to establish military control over the sovereign, over the territory of the sovereign Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, which is under attack, in order to create conditions for the political demarcation of the artificial construct called Herceg-Bosna, and that is the basis for giving this order. Have I accurately characterised what is found in paragraph number one?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written in paragraph number one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if I could have the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is 475, 475A for the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, does this number 02-33-867, dated the 16th of April 1993, deal with the subject matter that was found in the previous 194 Defence Exhibit, the previous order that was issued to the 303rd Mountain Brigade? Does it appear to be that very same order that is mentioned in Defence Exhibit 194?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Have you got this order, then, Mr. Harmon?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I indicated I was intending to introduce this order. I do have it and it is the order that is before Your Honours, Prosecutor's Exhibit 475.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We are pleased the order is here, Mr. President and Your Honours, but I have two comments, for the record: One is, this Court previously issued the binding order to the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina to produce documents, including this order, to the Defence. They declined to do so, instead providing it to the Prosecution, which I think would cause grave concerns to the Trial Chamber. Secondly, we don't know how long the Prosecutor has had it, but I will call the Court's attention to the fact we were not given this document under Rule 68. And yet, it says it is the 3rd Corps directing the 303rd Brigade of the BH army to, on the 16th of April, provide assistance, among other things, reading from paragraph one, provide assistance to our forces in the village of Putis, Jelinak, Loncari, Nadioci and Ahmici, directly addressing the issue of whether there were BH army forces in those locations. We should have gotten this document from the Prosecutor under Rule 68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would be glad to answer that, Mr. President. We received this document this morning, and this is an opportunity that we have had to present it to the Court and to counsel. So, in respect of the Rule 68 violation, Mr. President, I take serious issue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Obviously the Prosecutor's only strategic objectives took precedence over Rule 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't care to engage in a lengthy debate with Mr. Hayman on this particular issue, but this issue was raised by virtue of Mr. Hayman yesterday standing up and pointing to the exhibit he presented, 194, and indicating that the date was the 15th of April, as opposed to the 16th of April. That, Mr. President, piqued our interest in this issue and we pursued it. Mr. Hayman may not like the results, but we pursued the issue based on an issue that he raised in the course of his direct examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: It raises the question, Mr. President, what other exculpatory material is at the fingertips of the Prosecutor, but technically in the possession of the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and therefore, there is no obligation to produce it, they believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Mr. Hayman, I'm going to give you various answers about various things. In general, you are right in saying that the Prosecutor has to give you all the exculpatory evidence. But in this case that is the controversy that appeared yesterday. I think that's yesterday evening, I suppose, yesterday evening. The Office of the Prosecutor tried to find an explanation to this problem of dates. If this document was received this morning, they should have been given to you; but I would not like to make any lengthy polemics now. But the Prosecutor managed to have, very rapidly, the answer from one of the states in the region, but I will come back to my general remark on the three states in the region, although I do not want to go into the details. But whatever I said was my personal opinion and has nothing to do with my colleagues. There is something else that I would like to say, and I think this Trial Chamber has to have the dignified face towards Bosnia and Herzegovina. We now issued an order where we wanted to clear the matter of typewriters. We issued an order requesting Bosnia and Herzegovina to forward us the order 02-33-867, dated 16th of April; but I think, Mr. Harmon, that you have got it. So, it's an order that is already requested, it's already been fulfilled. Is this the same order?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: So, it is the same order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This is the order, Mr. President, about which there has been the considerable debate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Well, as my colleague just told me, that this Trial Chamber is really very satisfied that we have just issued an order and it was fulfilled straight away. This is very specific to the International Criminal Tribunal, but we are now going to put an end to this incident. Mr. Harmon, I would like to give you, once again, the possibility to ask the witness, and ask him the questions you wanted to ask him about this document, which is 475, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, 475 is the order that has been the subject of the controversy in the Defence Exhibit 194. I am submitting it on its face. It speaks for itself. I have no additional questions of this witness, and I would like to now turn to the last Defence Exhibit, 195A, if that could be placed in front of the witness, I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: We have 475 here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: 195, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Do we have 195? It must be in my documents. Yes, I see, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have some very brief questions about this document, please, Brigadier. First of all, this document was sent from the command of the Viteska Brigade. Can you tell me where the command of the Viteska Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In this time period, on this date I wouldn't know. I know that later on it was in the Isumarja (phoen) or forestry building, but I'm not sure it was there at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To whom was this particular document sent?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It was also sent, as usual, to the brigade commander and to me as the chief of the military intelligence service.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell me, by looking at this particular document, what form of transmission this document was sent? Are those fax numbers that faintly appear in the upper part of this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: This document could have been sent by fax, telephone. As far as I can tell, it was typed on the mechanical typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This document was sent during the period of combat on the 22nd of April, 1992 from a brigade headquarters to both the commander of the Central Bosnia Operational Zone and to your command?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It says, "To the command of the Central Bosnia Operative Military Intelligence Service," which means it was forwarded to Bila.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's fine. I understood your testimony to be that it was sent to Colonel Blaskic, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions with this document, Mr. President. I move to admit Prosecutor's Exhibit 467 through 475, and I have concluded my examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I have understood correctly, my learned colleague has tendered documents for admission. We have no objection, but we would like the statement from the Prosecutor that he received document 457 from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina, because in response to the same request the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina replied that it couldn't find it. 475A, that is the document we are referring to. We have no other objections regarding any of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: This is very important and very serious what you have just said, Mr. Nobilo. Can you provide the correspondence to the Registry of your request for this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: Of course, the reply. When did you ask for the document, when was it refused to you? A copy of your letter, a copy of the reply, and, of course, reference to the document to make sure that it was well identified. And we will see when we ask a state from the region, some parties get it very quickly and others don't get it. I'm saying it in this case for this state, but I may say the same for another state on another day. This is obviously in the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we will submit to you our entire correspondence regarding this matter. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Brigadier, this is the document you first saw when the Defence showed it to you. You didn't see it when you were making your own assessments.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Which document?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It is D194. It is the document we received from the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina we have been talking about for the last hour. The fact that the order of the 3rd Corps was issued on the 16th in the morning, before 12 o'clock, or on the 15th; does it change anything in respect of your conclusion that the BH army was planning an attack on the Lasva Valley?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No, it doesn't change anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Tell me, when a corps issues the command for an attack, does it, prior to that, issue a preparatory order and then the actual executive order; or does the executive order come immediately?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Before any activity is engaged in, either defensive or offensive operation, first a preparatory order is issued for the organisation of the unit, and after that comes the order for carrying out that operation, be it a defensive or offensive one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Therefore, a preparatory order had to have been issued at some time prior to the morning of the 16th of April, '93?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
