utterances.text: I will read to you Prosecutor Exhibit 475, the last one we just received, but something that the Prosecutor did not read to you. So I'm going to ask you what it means to you as a military man. I'm reading from the middle of the first paragraph. Let me read the whole paragraph, to give you the context, and I'm going to quote it. "The 3rd Corps orders that the commander of the 303rd Mountain Brigade will, from its troops, select one battalion," and then hand-written "with the second and third municipal staff of the Defence of Zenica," I can't read the handwriting, exactly, "from the present area of deployment, take them along the Zenica-Drivusa-Janjici-Janjicki Vrh-Gubanci axis, and capture and take control of the Defence region, grid point 957, in depth of the quota elevation point." We can't see the figure well. And then it says, now listen carefully, "To provide assistance to our forces in the village of Putis, Jelinak, Loncari, Nadioci, and Ahmici, our forces in those villages, in the event of an attack launched by the enemy, forcefully respond and embark on a counter-attack along Nadioci-Sivrino Selo axis." There is no need to quote further from this document. What can one deduce from this? That in the villages of Ahmici, Nadioci, Loncari, Jelinak, and Putis, there were elements of the BH army, according to this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a map as an exhibit. Could it be placed on the ELMO or given to the witness and distributed to their Honours and the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, could you get up, approach the map, and look to see whether a unit of the BH army in Ahmici is marked on this map? Will you tell us aloud, please?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes. I will look at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: This map is for the period the end of December '92, beginning of January '93. There are too many details for me to check, whether everything is exact, but according to the key, the blue colour indicates the Bosnian Serb army. So I'm asking you, once again --

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- whether the unit in Ahmici has been marked in blue. You may sit down. Can you describe how it was marked and which are the closest villages, so that we can identify exactly where Ahmici is, that is, the villages named on the map, because Ahmici is not, and how those units have been marked.

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Nadioci, Sivrino Selo.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: We are tendering this map

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number is D196.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Brigadier, would you please look with me, once again, at document D194 and the Prosecution document 475? Very well. That will do, so as not to waste time. Yesterday morning, or maybe in the afternoon, I'm not sure -- actually, it was in the morning, during the cross-examination by the Prosecution regarding the numbers of brigades, he said that he didn't have the document, but he also claimed that there was no 303rd Brigade from Zenica. By insight into document D194 and insight into document 475, what can you see from them? Is this evidence that the 303rd Brigade did exist in Zenica or not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes, that the 303rd Brigade exists, based in Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Therefore, the D194 document was issued by the 303rd Brigade, and document 475 was addressed to the brigade in Zenica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Will you please look at document D187? It is the assessment of the allies from the 6th of January, 1993. Will you look at the second page of the Croatian text, and at the bottom, can you tell me, in the fourth paragraph, how many soldiers did the unit accommodate in Silosu Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: How many men were at the front at Visoko and Turbe against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: 160 troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Is that what it says in that document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Tell me, where, according to this document, were the other soldiers, by far, the majority of those soldiers? What does that document tell us?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: It says that they were deployed in the villages with the weapons, which means they were not towards the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Does it say that there were 1.500 automatic and semi-automatic rifles, 20 anti-aircraft guns, 10 anti-air guns, 15 mortars, and three recoilless guns. Does it say that, too, in the document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Document D186, the diary of Enes Varupa, will you look through that document, please, and tell me, would you agree with me that the first date that appears in that document is the 17th of February, 1992, and the last date appearing there, look through it, please, is the 15th of April, 1992, the first and last dates that can be seen in this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Tell me, in the Vitez municipality where this document originated, between February 1992 and the middle of April 1992 or, rather, in that period, when was the BH army founded, on what date?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The BH army was established in this area on the 1st of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: But when did Territorial Defence units start or, rather, when did the war begin in Bosnia-Herzegovina? When was Sarajevo attacked?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: In April 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we say, then, that these were the first weeks that are mentioned in this diary, the first weeks of the formation of the Territorial Defence, the precursor of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina? We're talking about April '92. It has been correctly entered in the transcript as April '91. Can we say that, at the beginning, the Territorial Defence was poorly armed from February to April? Was this the generalised phenomenon?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we say that the main warehouses and depots captured by the HVO and the Territorial Defence were captured as of May that year, that is, after these dates?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we say that the equipment of the HVO and the Territorial Defence was significantly improved after May?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Exhibit D193, please. You remember this document, D193, whether it said the 14th of March or the 14th of April, '93. You said that it was the 14th of April. Why do you believe it is the 14th of April and not the 14th of March?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Because it can be seen here that the number 4 has been typed over number 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So these are numbers indicating months. Were they written by hand or by typewriter? Can you answer that?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: By typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you're concluding that the last figure typed was "4," and you come to the conclusion that it was in April?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can we see Prosecution Exhibit 467, the decision on the formation of the corps of the BH army? Exhibit 467. Brigadier, will you please look at this decision and tell us, does it represent an administrative basis for the formation of the corps, or at the moment that the decision was made, does that mean that the corps were formed? What would you say as the military man?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No. This is an administrative decision regarding the formation of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let me draw your attention to the second paragraph and, within the second paragraph, the third part listing the municipalities of the 3rd Corps. My question is: Was the 3rd Corps ever, to this day, in Banja Luka, Bosanska Dubica, Bosanska Gradiska?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Because then and now, this was the territory under the control of the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So an administrative decision and the wish is one thing, and the actual state of affairs is another?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Then, will you repeat, when, in effect, the 3rd Corps was formed?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps was formed on the 1st of December, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go on to document --

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Just the moment, please. We didn't take note of the number of the exhibit. Mr. Dubuisson, could you help us? It's the warning regarding behaviour towards joint property in Travnik, vehicles and communication vehicles. It is Exhibit 470.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Do you recall that the Prosecutor asked you about this? Could you explain to the Court what this means, attitude towards common property? Did the HVO ever control the maintenance institute in Travnik, that is, did it have full control of it itself? Who, in the end, took over this institute, this common property, and who managed it independently, eventually? Could you explain the confusion over this document?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, common property means that both the Territorial Defence and the HVO, at the time, had possession over this equipment. The HVO never had possession of this equipment on its own, nor did it use this equipment as an owner.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Who, in the end, threw who out and took full control over this institute?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: At the end, it was the BH army which took full control over this institute, as well as the barracks and all the equipment, and all the materiel remained in the possession of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: When you were testifying that the BH army had control over all the military industry, with the exception of the explosives factory in Vitez, is that true?

utterances.speaker: IVICA ZEKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: It is almost 5.30. Shall I proceed, Your Honours, Mr. President, because I have some more questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: I was just going to ask you that question. I think we shall not proceed, as you have the number of questions to put. In that case, I invite you to resume our work tomorrow afternoon. In line with our timetable, which is well-known to everyone, we will resume at 2.00 p.m. tomorrow afternoon for the end of the re-examination by the Defence, the questions of the Judges, after which, we shall have the Status Conference on various organisational matters regarding the Blaskic trial, and then we will hear the next witness. The hearing is adjourned until tomorrow at 2.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JORDA
utterances.text: 5.30 p.m. to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 23rd day of September, 1998 at 2.00 p.m. 23 24 25
